entities.summary:
Lazarillo de Tormes, published in 1554, is a seminal Spanish novella that marks the emergence of the picaresque genre, which chronicles the adventures of a roguish protagonist navigating a corrupt society. Set primarily in Spain, the text reflects the social conditions of the time, encapsulating the struggles of the lower classes and the hypocrisy of the upper echelons of society. Written anonymously, it is often attributed to Diego Hurtado de Mendoza, though its true authorship remains a topic of scholarly debate. This work significantly impacts literature, influencing not just Spanish narrative form but also the broader European literary tradition.

The novella tells the story of Lázaro, a young boy who becomes a servant to various masters, each representing different societal strata and moral failings. Through Lázaro's eyes, readers witness the injustices and absurdities of a society plagued by poverty and deceit. The narrative is structured as a first-person account, showcasing Lázaro's cunning and resilience as he learns to survive in an unforgiving world. This portrayal of social realism and the critique of established norms paved the way for modern literature, emphasizing character development and social commentary.

Lazarillo de Tormes' legacy is profound, establishing a narrative style that resonates through centuries, influencing writers such as Charles Dickens and Mark Twain. Its critique of societal hypocrisy and exploration of class struggles resonates in contemporary discussions about social justice and inequality. The novella was banned by the Spanish authorities shortly after its publication, indicating its potent social critique and the threat it posed to the status quo. The phrase 'I am not a man of great worth, but I am a man of great experience' encapsulates Lázaro's philosophical outlook and the broader human condition.
